deliberatelyUncovered.why: These titles are in the catalogue because people play them and want estimates, but an average frame rate at a preset is not a reproducible measurement for them. A fixture written anyway would be noise wearing the costume of evidence, and the calibrator cannot tell the difference. They are listed here so the Model Health screen can say 'excluded on purpose' rather than leaving them looking like an oversight.

games.factorio: The simulation is capped at 60 UPS and the meaningful metric is update rate on a large save, not frames. The catalogue already records fpsCap 60.
games.stellaris: Performance is measured in late-game turn time, not frames per second. A frame rate here says nothing about whether the game is playable.
games.civilization-vii: Turn-based; the number that matters is turn processing time on a large map.
games.cities-skylines-ii: Frame rate varies by more than 5x with city size and there is no standard save, so any single figure would be arbitrary.
games.star-citizen: Permanent alpha. Server-side performance dominates the client frame rate and both change between patches, so a figure is stale within weeks.
games.escape-from-tarkov: Map- and raid-dependent with no repeatable scene; Streets of Tarkov and Factory differ by a factor of two on identical hardware.
games.arma-reforger: Scenario- and server-dependent. Player count and AI load move the result far more than the hardware does.
